 Gold Futures Rise to Rs 1.42 Lakh on Strong Spot Demand
 By Rediff Money Desk , New Delhi 
 1 Minute Read Listen to Article 
 Share:     
 Oct 26, 2026 11:04
 x 
 Gold futures surged to Rs 1,42,841 per 10 grams on Monday, driven by fresh speculative positions and firm spot demand on the Multi Commodity Exchange. Key Points
 Gold futures rose by Rs 817 to Rs 1,42,841 per 10 grams on Monday.
 The price increase was attributed to firm spot demand and fresh speculative positions.
 Trading occurred on the Multi Commodity Exchange with a turnover of 811 lots.
 International gold futures also saw a rise, reaching USD 4,014.81 per ounce in New York.
 New Delhi, Oct 26 (PTI) Gold prices on Monday rose by Rs 817 to Rs 1,42,841 per 10 grams in futures trade as speculators created fresh positions on firm spot demand.
 On the Multi Commodity Exchange, the yellow metal contract for December delivery traded higher by Rs 817, or 0.58 per cent, at Rs 1,42,841 per 10 grams in a business turnover of 811 lots.
 Fresh positions by market participants led to a rise in precious metal's prices, analysts said.
 Gold futures rose 0.47 per cent to USD 4,014.81 per ounce in New York. -->
